obra-dinn.title: Return of the Obra Dinn (Lucas Pope, 2018)

tiny-glade.description: Warm low sun with soft real-time GI and deep soft AO; shadows fill with sky colour, so nothing goes grey.
Few materials (stone, plaster, terracotta, grass, water) reused everywhere; coherence comes from the small set, not from rules.
Ivy, flowers and moss creep onto whatever you build: the world answers the builder with colour.
Almost no UI colour; the world is the only saturated thing on screen.
The particular cottage, castle and rooftile designs.

bricktales.description: Every colour is a real brick colour, so any build is in-gamut by construction: coherence enforced by the parts list.
The stud repeats at every scale (ground, trees, water, characters): one motif binds the world.
Each scene is a diorama on a base, held like a toy.
Each world (jungle, desert, city) swaps the brick palette but keeps the grammar.
LEGO brick shapes, minifigures and branding.

dorfromantik.description: Each tile type owns a hue family: wheat gold, forest green, water blue, red-roofed villages. You read the scoring rules from colour plus shape at a glance.
An 'ideal and harmonic interpretation' of rural landscape, painted rather than realistic (developers, Game Developer).
The board fades to a pale void at its edge. Against our house rule (nothing masks the world).
The particular tile artwork and village models.

9-kings.description: Each king has a colour; whose plot and whose army it is reads from hue across the board.
A dark surround makes the small bright kingdom tiles pop: the backdrop is the quietest value.
Crisp pixel-art units at small scale; silhouettes before detail.
The kings, card art and unit sprites.

besiege.description: Wood, iron, canvas and brass parts: the medieval-engineer motif makes any contraption look like it belongs.
Muted, low-detail levels so the player's machine is the most readable thing on screen.
Part material says function (metal for joints and blades, wood for structure, cloth for sails).
The particular block shapes and level art.

dont-starve.description: Ink outlines on paper-cutout figures; 'sketchy newspaper cartoon' (developers, Game Developer).
Night drains the world to black and only firelight keeps warm colour: light radius is survival.
Low sanity desaturates and distorts the screen (meta) and wakes shadow creatures (diegetic).
Each season recolours the whole world: autumn amber, winter blue-white, spring green, summer dust.
Triangle-heavy, spindly silhouettes signal threat; a horror shape language we keep out of a kids' game.
Wilson, the character designs and Burton/Gorey-like look.

this-war-of-mine.description: Charcoal and sepia, 'old sepia photography' (80.lv interview). Colour is almost absent, so any warm hue (a stove, a candle) carries enormous weight.
Unexplored rooms are dark and hatched; what you know is lit.
Scarcity of colour as tone: the lesson is that accents are precious, not that we want grey.
The charcoal character portraits and war imagery.

steamworld-dig.description: Underground layers change hue with depth (warm dirt, then cooler rock): you know how deep you are from colour.
Ore colour and sparkle say value; gems are the most saturated thing underground.
The lamp's light radius is the palette: lit warm, unlit near-black.
Rusty and the steambot western designs.

firewatch.description: Bold colours in distinct depth layers separated by fog; flat shapes with strong silhouettes (GDC 2015, Jane Ng).
A colour script tied to story beats; the sky drives the palette and changes as you move ('no birthday-party colours when you want spooky').
Olly Moss's poster look and the particular landscapes.

journey.description: The palette walks the story: gold sand, pink sunset, blue underground, white snow, gold again. Colour is the plot.
Red cloth is the only red: the scarf and banners mean 'flight and companionship'. A reserved hue.

townscaper.description: The player picks house colours from a swatch row tuned to similar value and chroma, so every choice harmonises. The exact pattern a child's picker needs.
Rules grow arches, stairs and roofs from the grid; the motif emerges from the grammar.

monument-valley.description: Each chapter is its own pastel palette over the same isometric grammar: a place dialect.
Faces lit by flat value steps (top light, left mid, right dark), so form reads with no texture.
Ida's white cone hat and the specific architecture.

a-short-hike.description: Golden feathers are the most saturated gold in the world and always mean 'climb further'. Reserved accent.
3D rendered at low resolution with a warm grade: detail density held down so the whole island reads as one thing.
Claire and the island's character designs.

obra-dinn.description: Two colours and dithering: the most extreme proof that coherence comes from a constraint everything obeys.
